_meta.feast: The Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross
_meta._note: Single-canon (Tone 8 by Cosmas the Monk); each katavasia repeats its own ode's irmos (no separate katavasiae text). Lord's feast — but Having Beheld IS sung per OCA rubric (`includeHavingBeheld: true`). Magnificat replaced by feast-specific Ode 9 refrain (`skipMagnificat: true`). Veneration stichera sung after the Great Doxology are not yet captured.

troparion.text:
O Lord, save Thy people,
and bless Thine inheritance!
Grant victories to the Orthodox Christians
over their adversaries;
and by virtue of Thy Cross,
preserve Thy habitation!
troparion.label: Troparion of the Elevation

kontakion.text:
As Thou wast voluntarily raised upon the Cross for our sake,
grant mercy to those who are called by Thy Name, O Christ God;
make all Orthodox Christians glad by Thy power,
granting them victories over their adversaries
by bestowing on them the invincible trophy, Thy weapon of peace!
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the Elevation

sedalion.text:
We venerate the wood of Thy Cross, O Lover of mankind,
for upon it Thou wast nailed, O Life of all.
O Savior, Thou hast opened Paradise
to the thief who turned to Thee in faith,
counting him worthy of blessedness
when he confessed Thee crying: "O Lord, remember me."
Accept us like him, as we cry: "We all have sinned,
in Thy merciful kindness despise us not."
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 1)

sedalion.text:
No sooner had the wood of Thy Cross been set up, O Christ,
the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord.
For that which hell had swallowed up so eagerly,
it let go in trembling.
Thou hast shown us Thy salvation, O Holy One, and we glorify Thee.
Have mercy on us, O Son of God!
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 2)

magnification.refrain:
We magnify Thee,
O Christ, the Giver of life,
and we honor Thy precious Cross
by which Thou hast saved us
from the bondage of the enemy.
verses: O Lord, judge those who offend me; fight against those who fight against me! (Ps. 34:1)
Take hold of shield and buckler, and stand up for my help. (Ps. 34:2)

prokeimenon.refrain: All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
prokeimenon.verse: Sing to the Lord a new song, for the Lord has done marvelous things.

gospel._note: The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.

postGospelSticheron.text:
O Cross of Christ,
the hope of Christians,
guide of those who have gone astray,
haven of the storm-tossed,
victory in warfare,
the safeguard of the inhabited earth,
physician of the sick,
resurrection of the dead:
have mercy on us.
postGospelSticheron.label: Idiomelon of the Elevation

canon._katavasiaeNote: Each ode's katavasia repeats that ode's own irmos.

ode1.irmos:
Moses traced out a cross,
as with his staff he divided the Red Sea in two,
so that Israel could go across on foot;
and then striking it again crosswise,
and uniting it over Pharaoh and his chariots,
he inscribed the Invincible Weapon.
Therefore let us sing to Christ our God, for He has been glorified.

ode3.irmos:
The rod of Aaron is an image of this mystery,
for when it budded it revealed who should be the priest;
and for the Church, which before was barren,
the Tree of the Cross has blossomed forth
for her strength and firm foundation.

ode4.irmos:
I have heard the mystery of Thy dispensation, O Lord,
I have meditated on Thy works
and have glorified Thy Godhead.
ode4.katavasia:

ode5.irmos:
O thrice-blessed Tree, on which Christ the King and Lord was stretched!
Through thee the one who deceived us through a tree has fallen,
caught by the bait of God, Who was nailed to thee in the flesh,
and Who grants peace to our souls.
ode5.katavasia:

ode6.irmos:
In the belly of the sea monster, Jonah stretched out his hands in the form of a cross,
plainly prefiguring the saving Passion.
When he emerged from there on the third day,
he prefigured the transcendent Resurrection of Christ our God,
Who was nailed to the Cross in the flesh
and by His rising on the third day enlightened the world.

ode7.irmos:
The senseless decree of the impious tyrant,
spewing threats and blasphemy hateful to God,
brought the people to confusion.
Yet the three Children could not be frightened
either by the brutal fury or the roaring fire,
but in the wind, moist with dew, that blew against it,
they stood together, and they sang:
"O praised above all, blessed art Thou,
our God, and the God of our Fathers!"

ode8.irmos:
O Children, equal in number to the Trinity,
bless God the Father, the Creator;
praise the Word, Who descended and changed the fire to dew,
and exalt above all, to all ages,
the All-Holy Spirit, Who gives life to all!

ode9.irmos:
Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the most precious Cross of the Lord!

Heirmos: Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Theotokos,
who, though untilled, hast brought forth Christ;
through Him the life-bearing wood of the Cross was planted on earth.
Now at its Exaltation,
as we bow in worship before it, we magnify thee.

exapostilarion.text:
The Cross is the guardian of the whole earth.
The Cross is the beauty of the Church.
The Cross is the strength of Orthodox Christians.
The Cross is the support of the faithful.
The Cross is the glory of the angels,
and the wounder of the demons.
exapostilarion.label: Exapostilarion of the Elevation

stichera.verse: Praise Him for His mighty deeds; praise Him according to His exceeding greatness! (Ps. 150:2)
stichera.text:
Oh, most glorious wonder!
The life-bearing Tree, the all-holy Cross
today is raised up on high and shown to the world.
All the ends of the earth give glory;
all the demons are struck with terror.
Oh, what a gift is bestowed on mortals.
Through the Cross, save our souls, O Christ,
as Thou alone art compassionate!

stichera.verse: Praise Him with trumpet sound; praise Him with lute and harp! (Ps. 150:3)
Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and pipe! (Ps. 150:4)
stichera.text:
Oh, most glorious wonder!
The Cross that carried the Most High
like a cluster of grapes filled with life
today is seen raised above the earth.
Through this we have all been drawn to God,
and death is finally swallowed up.
O immaculate Wood!
Through thee we enjoy the immortal food of Eden
as we give glory to Christ!

stichera.verse: Praise Him with sounding cymbals; praise Him with loud clashing cymbals! Let everything that breathes praise the Lord! (Ps. 150:5)
stichera.text:
Oh, most glorious wonder!
The length and breadth of the Cross is equal to heaven,
for by divine grace it sanctifies the universe.
By the Cross, pagan nations are overcome.
By the Cross the scepters of kings are firmly established.
O divine ladder, by which we go up to heaven,
exalting Christ the Lord in song!

doxastikon.text:
Today the Cross of the Lord comes forth;
the faithful welcome it with longing
and receive healing of soul and body and of infirmity.
Let us kiss it with joy and fear:
fear because our sin, since we are unworthy,
but joy because of the salvation given to the world
by Christ the Lord Who was nailed upon it,
Who has great mercy.
doxastikon.author: Doxastikon of the Elevation

troparionAfterDoxology.text:

Grant victories to the Orthodox Christians
